forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 25%. CAISI announced May 5 expansion of pre-deployment evaluation agreements to Google DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI (joining 2024 OpenAI/Anthropic partners), formalising a US government early-access regime that adds disclosure friction before any unilateral AGI declaration. Anthropic's May 9 Claude Mythos Preview launch is a narrow cybersecurity tool (Project Glasswing), not an AGI claim. No new declarations from any frontier lab in past 24 hours. Resolution window now ~32 months. Time decay + heavier oversight nudges the estimate down marginally.
forecasts.base_rate: ~22% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and superforecaster surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Anthropic Colossus 1 (220k+ GPU) compute lock-in continues to anchor 2027-28 capability gains (+2pp)
Amodei reiterated 2026-27 human-level timeline on May 8 White House meeting (+1pp)
Microsoft/OpenAI revised contract: independent expert panel verifies AGI declaration, lowering one barrier (+1pp)
Continued benchmark saturation across coding, math and agentic tasks (+1pp)
factors_down: AGI definition contested; resolution requires lab declaration or 3+ researchers (-3pp)
Resolution window narrowed to ~32 months from 30+ at start of forecast (-1pp)
CAISI pre-deployment regime expanded to all big labs (May 5) increases declaration friction (-2pp)
Polymarket OpenAI-AGI-by-2027 still in single digits (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Colossus 1-trained Anthropic models cross a self-declared AGI threshold in 2027-28
How CAISI early-access regime affects strategic timing of declarations
Whether 'agentic' capability gates substitute for an AGI announcement

update_triggers.up: A frontier lab publicly declares AGI; or 3+ leading researchers publicly endorse achieved status
update_triggers.down: Capability plateau at next-gen frontier; major lab walks back AGI timeline; CAISI imposes formal pre-disclosure delay

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 24%. May 6 reporting confirms OpenAI and Anthropic both rolling out consultancy-style enterprise offerings directly competing with strategy houses (Project Glasswing security advisory, GPT-5 'analyst pyramid' tier). McKinsey's December 2025 10% non-client headcount cut continues to roll through; Bloomberg April 15 piece confirmed BCG/Bain/McKinsey reshaping entry-level hiring around AI. Cumulative trajectory now closer to a 33% impairment threshold by 2030 than 30 days ago, but still requires multiple credible analyses attributing primarily to AI - which has not yet emerged in mainstream coverage.
forecasts.base_rate: ~15% for industry-wide ≥33% disruption in a ~5-year window across services sectors historically
factors_up: OpenAI/Anthropic May 2026 consultancy-style enterprise rollout (+2pp)
McKinsey 10% non-client cut continuing; BCG/Bain entry-level hiring reshaped (+1pp)
150 ex-MBB consultants reportedly training AI to do entry-level tasks (Bloomberg) (+1pp)
Big-four (KPMG, Deloitte) shifting workforce design around AI in 2025 (+1pp)
factors_down: Resolution requires 'primarily attributed to AI by 2+ credible analyses' - high bar (-3pp)
Senior-partner relationship-driven revenue is harder to disintermediate (-2pp)
Consultancies are also AI implementers; revenue redistribution rather than collapse (-2pp)
Headcount cuts so far concentrated in non-client/back-office roles, not core consulting (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 2027-28 sees a credible industry analysis explicitly attributing ≥33% loss to AI
Whether MBB firms can re-price upward to offset volume loss
How strategy work vs implementation work decompose in headline 'consultancy revenue' metrics

update_triggers.up: Reuters/FT/Bloomberg explicit ≥33%-attributed-to-AI analysis; MBB total revenue YoY decline >10%
update_triggers.down: MBB revenue grows in 2026 results; consultancies successfully re-price AI-augmented engagements

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. May 7-8 local elections delivered a historic Labour wipeout: 1,496 councillors lost, control of 38 councils gone, polling near 20% - a post-war low. Reform UK won 26-27% of vote, took councils including Sunderland, Suffolk, Essex, Havering and Newcastle-under-Lyme. CNN/CBS framing: 'historic shift in British politics'. Starmer says he will not resign. Labour MPs publicly calling for resignation. The local results were already largely priced in to the 1% estimate; no reason to revise further down (already at floor). Hold.
forecasts.base_rate: ~10% historical reversion for governments down 25+ pp in mid-term polling
factors_up: Long runway to next GE (up to Dec 2029) - economic recovery possible (+1pp)
FPTP system with split right-wing vote (Reform vs Conservative) could let Labour win on low share (+1pp)
No PM has been removed by Labour party machinery in 125 years - leadership stable (+0pp)
factors_down: Labour polling ~20%, Reform ~26-27% - structural lead (-3pp)
Local elections May 7-8 delivered historic wipeout, 1,496 councillors lost (-2pp)
Starmer approval -47% - lowest for any PM since polling began at this point in cycle (-2pp)
Internal Labour party calls for Starmer resignation - leadership instability (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates the right or fragments under coalition pressure
Whether Starmer is replaced and by whom
Whether Labour can rebuild a coherent economic narrative before 2029

update_triggers.up: Reform internal split; Labour leadership change with polling bump; major economic recovery
update_triggers.down: Reform formal merger with Conservatives; Labour polling falls below 18%

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 76%. The 2035 horizon (~9 years out) is largely insensitive to single-day declaration friction events. Same May 5 CAISI expansion + May 9 Mythos news that nudged 2030 marginally lower do not materially shift 2035 - over a decade window, capability accumulation dominates declaration timing. Most expert surveys (Metaculus, Cotra, Karnofsky) cluster 60-85% by 2035; Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepMind leadership all publicly endorse AGI within decade. Hold.
forecasts.base_rate: ~70% from Metaculus 'AGI by 2035' aggregator and median expert surveys
factors_up: Compute scaling (Colossus 1, OpenAI Stargate, Google TPU buildout) continues +0.5 OOM/year (+3pp)
Three frontier labs publicly targeting AGI within decade (+2pp)
Algorithmic efficiency gains (post-training, RL, mixture-of-experts) compounding (+1pp)
factors_down: Resolution requires lab declaration or 3+ researchers - subjective threshold (-3pp)
Possible regulatory or compute-export bottleneck before 2030 (-2pp)
Energy/grid constraints could throttle 2027-30 build-out (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 'AGI' is declared meaningfully earlier than 2030 or pushed past 2035
Whether Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot) accelerate or decelerate timeline
Whether compute scaling laws hold beyond 2028

update_triggers.up: Two frontier labs declare AGI; benchmark saturation across all major suites
update_triggers.down: Capability plateau in 2027-28 frontier models; major export controls cut off compute

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. AEI May 8 update: PLAN responded to Balikatan 2026 exercises with two major South China Sea / West Pacific deployments - signalling but not escalating. Taiwan LY passed special 780B NTD defense budget May 8 despite KMT efforts to shrink it. March US intelligence assessment maintained that China is not committed to a 2027 Taiwan invasion. Polymarket implies 92.5% probability against invasion-by-2026; my central estimate covers a ~44-month window through Jan 2030. No structural change - hold.
forecasts.base_rate: ~7% reference class of major-power maritime blockades/amphibious assaults in ~4-year windows since 1990
factors_up: PLA Joint Sword exercises now annual standard; capability bar dropping (+1pp)
Bashi Channel sensor/beacon emplacement consistent with blockade prep (+1pp)
Xi 2027 PLA modernisation deadline still in window (+1pp)
Taiwan presidential dynamics could provide pretext (+1pp)
factors_down: US intel: PRC not committed to 2027 invasion (-2pp)
Taiwan passing 780B NTD defense budget May 8 raises invasion cost (-1pp)
PLA logistics/training gaps still flagged in 2026 assessments (-1pp)
Xi domestic economy/property crisis complicates risk calculus (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether 'gray zone' actions (cyber, customs blockade) cross the >72hr threshold
Whether US/Japan/Australia deterrent posture holds through 2027-29
Whether 2028 Taiwan election produces pretext for action

update_triggers.up: PLA mobilisation exceeding any 2024-26 exercise scale; PRC declaration of customs control over Taiwan Strait
update_triggers.down: Cross-strait political detente; Xi succession event reducing risk appetite

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. ONS March 2026 CPI release: 3.3% YoY (up from 3.0% in February). Bank of England April MPR explicitly states inflation 'likely to be higher later this year as effects of higher energy prices pass through'; April near-term projection revised up by 1.4pp - Q3 2026 CPI now expected at 3.3%. With ~7 monthly prints remaining before deadline (April-October 2026 prints, published May-Nov), CPI would need to drop >1.3pp in a single month - implausible without a deflationary shock. Effectively at floor.
forecasts.base_rate: Single-month CPI drops >1.3pp from a 3.3% level: roughly 2% historical frequency
factors_up: Possible energy price collapse (oil >$30/bbl decline) (+1pp)
Sharp GBP appreciation could cut imported goods inflation (+0pp)
Possible base-effect month if energy prints drop sharply (+0pp)
factors_down: BoE April MPR: CPI expected 3.3% in Q3 2026 (-2pp)
March CPI 3.3% - already 1.3pp above target (-1pp)
Services inflation running hotter than expected (-1pp)
Middle East conflict pushing oil higher, not lower (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether a sudden recession-driven demand shock arrives in Q3-Q4 2026
Whether BoE accelerates rate cuts in response to GE political pressure
Whether ONS revises methodology in a way that lowers headline

update_triggers.up: Oil collapse to <$50/bbl; UK enters technical recession with rapid disinflation
update_triggers.down: April CPI release prints ≥3.5%; BoE upward revision in May report

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 99%. April 2026 disclosures: Anthropic ARR $30B (per SaaStr/Sacra/Epoch AI - 1,400% YoY growth), OpenAI ARR $24B (confirmed by company at $2B/month). Even if OpenAI's gross-vs-net dispute lops $8B off Anthropic's headline figure (their preferred view: ~$22B Anthropic + $24B OpenAI = $46B), trajectory still clears $70B comfortably. Hold near ceiling.

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 41%. OBR March 2026 EFO maintains medium-term productivity at 0.8% (revised down from 1.1% in November 2025) plus AI-attributed productivity boost of 0.2pp by forecast horizon, giving ~1.0% productivity growth. Add labour supply growth declining from recent highs to ~0.5% by 2030 and you get headline GDP growth in the ~1.3-1.5% range - precisely on the threshold. The question hinges on whether AI productivity uplift exceeds OBR's cautious 0.2pp central case (Acemoglu 0.05pp vs Goldman 1.5pp range). Genuinely two-sided.
forecasts.base_rate: UK GDP growth >1.5% in any 10-year window since 2010: ~55%
factors_up: AI productivity uplift could exceed OBR's 0.2pp central case (+5pp)
Population growth (net migration) supports labour supply contribution (+2pp)
Catch-up potential from 2010s productivity stagnation (+2pp)
factors_down: OBR March 2026 productivity revised down to 0.8% in medium term (-3pp)
Labour supply growth declining to ~0.5% by 2030 (-2pp)
Per-person GDP forecast only 1.1% per OBR (-2pp)
Energy transition and demographic ageing create persistent headwinds (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Magnitude and distribution of AI productivity gains across UK economy
Net migration policy trajectory under post-2029 government
Whether 2030s public investment lifts capital deepening sufficiently

update_triggers.up: OBR or BoE upward revision to productivity forecasts; AI implementation evidence
update_triggers.down: Further downward productivity revisions; recession in late 2020s
